Moksha.fact: Realization of anatta (anatman) is essential to Buddhist nirvana.

Moksha.fact: For example, Keval jnana or kaivalya ("state of Absolute"), Apavarga, Nihsreyasa, Paramapada, Brahmabhava, Brahmajnana and Brahmi sthiti.

Moksha.fact: Yoga gained wide acceptance in ancient India, its ideas and practices became part of many religious schools in Hinduism, including those that were very different from Sāmkhya.

Moksha.fact: Yoga, or mārga (meaning "way" or "path"), in Hinduism is widely classified into four spiritual approaches.

Moksha.fact: The first mārga is Jñāna Yoga, the way of knowledge. The second mārga is Bhakti Yoga, the way of loving devotion to God.

Moksha.fact: For example, the Ekasarana dharma denies the sayujya form of mukti, where the complete absorption in God deprives jiva of the sweetness and bliss associated with bhakti.

Moksha.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Moksha.fact: Madhavadeva begins the Namghoxa by declaring his admiration for devotees who do not prefer mukti.

Moksha.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Moksha.question: Advaita holds there is no being/non-being distinction between Atman, _____, and Paramatman
Moksha.fact: Advaita holds there is no being/non-being distinction between Atman, Brahman, and Paramatman. True knowledge is a direct, permanent realization that the Atman and Brahman are one.

Moksha.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Moksha.question: True knowledge is a direct, permanent realization that the Atman and _____ are one
Moksha.fact: Advaita holds there is no being/non-being distinction between Atman, Brahman, and Paramatman. True knowledge is a direct, permanent realization that the Atman and Brahman are one.

Moksha.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Moksha.question: Vivekachudamani, which literally means "_____ of Discriminatory Reasoning", is a book devoted to moksa in Advaita Vedanta philosophy
Moksha.fact: Vivekachudamani, which literally means "Crown Jewel of Discriminatory Reasoning", is a book devoted to moksa in Advaita Vedanta philosophy.

Moksha.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Moksha.fact: To Ramanuja, avidya is a focus on the self, and vidya is a focus on a loving god. Such ideas, claims Ramanuja, decay to materialism, hedonism and self worship.

Moksha.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Moksha.fact: Jivanmukti is a state that transforms the nature, attributes, and behaviors of an individual, according to these ancient texts of Hindu philosophy.

Moksha.fact: With release comes Nirvana (Pali: Nibbana), "blowing out", "quenching", or "becoming extinguished" of the fires of the passions and of self-view. Nirvana ends the cycle of Dukkha and rebirth in the six realms of saṃsāra.

Moksha.fact: In Jainism, it is believed to be a stage beyond ethical perfection, states Paul Dundas, because they can perform physical and mental activities such as teach, without accruing karma that leads to rebirth.

Moksha.fact: In the Digambara tradition of Jainism, women must live an ethical life and gain karmic merit to be reborn as a man, because only males can achieve spiritual liberation.

Sutra.fact: This may reflect a derivation from Vedic or Sanskrit sūkta (well spoken), rather than from sūtra (thread). The word is related to sūci (Sanskrit: सूचि) meaning "needle, list", and sūnā (Sanskrit: सूना) meaning "woven".

Sutra.fact: A sūtra is different from other components such as Shlokas, Anuvyakhayas, and Vyakhyas found in ancient Indian literature.

Sutra.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Sutra.fact: The oldest manuscripts that have survived into the modern era that contain extensive sutras are part of the Vedas, dated from the late 2nd millennium BCE through to the mid 1st millennium BCE. In the history of Indian literature, large compilations of sutras, in diverse fields of knowledge, have been traced to the period from 600 BCE to 200 BCE (mostly after Buddha and Mahavira), and this has been called the "sutras period".

Sutra.fact: This period followed the more ancient Chhandas period, Mantra period and Brahmana period.

Sutra.fact: It is one of the foundational texts of the Vedānta school of Hindu philosophy.

Sutra.fact: The Kalpa Sūtra is, for example, a Jain text that includes monastic rules, as well as biographies of the Jain Tirthankaras.

Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Vedanta.question: The _____ was One of the six orthodox traditions of Hindu philosophy.
Vedanta.fact: Vedanta (; Sanskrit: वेदान्त, IAST: Vedānta [ʋeːdɑ́ːntɐ]), also called Uttara Mīmāṃsā, is one of the six orthodox (āstika) schools of Hindu philosophy and textual exegesis. The word Vedanta means 'conclusion of the Vedas,' and encompasses the ideas that emerged from, or aligned and reinterpreted, the speculations and enumerations contained in the Upanishads, focusing, with varying emphasis, on devotion, knowledge, and liberation.

Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Vedanta.question: The influence of Vedanta is prominent in the sacred literatures of Hinduism, such as the various Puranas, Samhitas, Agamas and _____ ..
Vedanta.fact: The influence of Vedanta is prominent in the sacred literatures of Hinduism, such as the various Puranas, Samhitas, Agamas and Tantras ..

Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Vedanta.question: The Upanishads may be regarded as the end of _____ in different senses: They were the last literary products of the Vedic period
Vedanta.fact: Anta (अन्त) — meaning "end." The word Vedanta literally means the end of the Vedas and originally referred to the Upanishads. Vedanta is concerned with the jñānakāṇḍa or knowledge section of the vedas which is called the Upanishads.

Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Vedanta.question: They represent the pinnacle of _____ philosophy
Vedanta.fact: The Upanishads may be regarded as the end of Vedas in different senses: They were the last literary products of the Vedic period. They represent the pinnacle of Vedic philosophy.

Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Vedanta.question: They were taught and debated last, in the _____ (ascetic) stage
Vedanta.fact: They were taught and debated last, in the Sannyasa (ascetic) stage.

Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Vedanta.question: It is also called _____ Mīmāṃsā, which means the "latter enquiry" or "higher enquiry"; and is often contrasted with Pūrva Mīmāṃsā, the "former enquiry" or "primary enquiry"
Vedanta.fact: It is also called Uttara Mīmāṃsā, which means the "latter enquiry" or "higher enquiry"; and is often contrasted with Pūrva Mīmāṃsā, the "former enquiry" or "primary enquiry". Pūrva Mīmāṃsā deals with the karmakāṇḍa or ritualistic section (the Samhita and Brahmanas) in the Vedas while Uttara Mīmāṃsā concerns itself with the deeper questions of the relation between humans and Divine or Absolute reality.

Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Vedanta.fact: The various traditions give their own, specific exegesis of the Upaniṣads, the Bhagavadgītā, and the Brahma Sūtras (known as the three canonical sources).

Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Vedanta.fact: Scripture (Sruti Śabda) is the main reliable source of knowledge (pramana).

Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Vedanta.question: Rejection of _____ and Jainism and conclusions of the other Vedic schools (Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Samkhya, Yoga, and, to some extent, the Purva Mimamsa)
Vedanta.fact: Rejection of Buddhism and Jainism and conclusions of the other Vedic schools (Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Samkhya, Yoga, and, to some extent, the Purva Mimamsa).

Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Vedanta.question: All prominent _____ teachers, including Shankara, Bhaskara, Ramanuja, Madhva, Nimbarka, and Vallabha wrote commentaries on these three sources
Vedanta.fact: All prominent Vedantic teachers, including Shankara, Bhaskara, Ramanuja, Madhva, Nimbarka, and Vallabha wrote commentaries on these three sources. The Bhagavadgītā, with its syncretism of Samkhya, Yoga, and Upanishadic thought, has also been a significant influence on Vedantic thought.

Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

The conclusion is that with regard to supernatural matters, Scripture alone is the epistemic authority and that reasoning is to be used only in support of Scripture' [Śrī Bhāṣya 2.1.12].

Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Vedanta.fact: Aparā or Lower Brahman: The Brahman with qualities defined as aparā Brahman or saguṇa Brahman.

Vedanta.fact: Aparā or Lower Brahman: The Brahman with qualities defined as aparā Brahman or saguṇa Brahman. The saguṇa Brahman is endowed with attributes and represents the personal God of religion.

Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Vedanta.fact: The oneness of the Supreme Reality is understood in the sense of an organic unity (vishistaikya).

Vedanta.fact: According to Viśiṣṭādvaita (qualified non-dualism), Jīvātman is different from Īśvara, though eternally connected with Him as His mode. According to Dvaita (dualism), the Jīvātman is totally and always different from Brahman / Īśvara.

Vedanta.fact: According to Shuddhadvaita (pure non-dualism), the Jīvātman and Brahman are identical; both, along with the changing empirically observed universe being Krishna.

Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Nimbarka.fact: It supports the bhedābheda school of Vedānta, which advocates the view of a relationship of simultaneous unity and diversity between Brahman, the individual soul (jīva) and the universe (jagat).

Nimbarka.fact: Sundara bhaṭṭācharya has authored a commentary on this work titled Mantrārtharahasya. The Prapannakalpavallī explains the mukunda śaraṇāgati mantra.

Nimbarka.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Nimbarka.fact: Sundara bhaṭṭācharya has authored a commentary on this work titled Mantrārtharahasya. On this, Sundara bhaṭṭācharya has written an extensive commentary titled Prapannasuratarumañjarī.

Vallabha.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Vallabha.question: The _____ was Hindu philosopher (1478–1530).
Vallabha.fact: Vallabha, also called Vallabhācārya or Vallabha Dīkṣita (May 7, 1478 – July 7, 1530 CE), was the founder of the Kr̥ṣṇa-centered Puṣṭimārga sect of Vaishnavism, and propounded the philosophy of Śuddhādvaita. Born into a Telugu Brahmin family, Vallabha studied Hindu philosophy from an early age, then traveled throughout the Indian subcontinent, particularly the Braj (Vraja) region, for over 20 years.

Vallabha.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Vallabha.question: He became one of the important leaders of the devotional _____ movement
Vallabha.fact: He became one of the important leaders of the devotional Bhakti movement.

Vallabha.fact: He authored many texts including but not limited to, the Aṇubhāṣya (his commentary on the Brahma Sutras), Ṣoḍaśa Grantha or sixteen tracts and several commentaries on the Bhāgavata Purāṇa.

Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Madhvacharya.question: The _____ was 13th century Hindu Dvaita philosopher.
Madhvacharya.fact: Madhvacharya (IAST: Madhvācārya; pronounced [mɐdʱʋaːˈtɕaːrjɐ]; 1199–1278 CE or 1238–1317 CE), also called Purna Prajna (IAST: Pūrṇa-Prajña) and Ānanda Tīrtha, was an Indian philosopher, theologian and the chief proponent of the Dvaita (dualism) school of Vedanta. Madhvacharya was born at Pajaka near Udupi on the west coast of Karnataka state in 13th-century India.

Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Madhvacharya.fact: Madhva called his philosophy Tattvavāda meaning "arguments from a realist viewpoint".

Madhvacharya.fact: As a teenager, he became a Sanyasi (monk) joining Brahma-sampradaya guru Achyutapreksha, of the Ekadandi order.

Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Madhvacharya.fact: Madhva studied the classics of Hindu philosophy, and wrote commentaries on the Principal Upanishads, the Bhagavad Gita and the Brahma Sutras (Prasthanatrayi), and is credited with thirty seven works in Sanskrit.

Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Madhvacharya.fact: His greatest work is considered to be the Anuvyakhyana, a philosophical supplement to his bhasya on the Brahma Sutras composed with a poetic structure.

Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Madhvacharya.fact: He toured India several times, visiting places such as Badrinath, Bengal, Varanasi, Dwaraka, Goa and Kanyakumari, engaging in philosophical debates and visiting Hindu centres of learning.

Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Madhvacharya.question: His school's theistic dualism teachings disagreed with the monist teachings of the other two most influential schools of _____ based on Advaita's nondualism and Vishishtadvaita's qualified nondualism
Madhvacharya.fact: His school's theistic dualism teachings disagreed with the monist teachings of the other two most influential schools of Vedanta based on Advaita's nondualism and Vishishtadvaita's qualified nondualism. Madhvacharya.fact: Madhva studied the Upanishads and the Advaita literature, but was unconvinced by its nondualism philosophy of oneness of human soul and god, had frequent disagreements with his guru, left the monastery, and began his own tattvavada movement based on dualism premises of Dvi – asserting that human soul and god (as Vishnu) are two different things. Madhvacharya.fact: Of these, the most referred to and most authentic is the sixteen cantos Sanskrit biography Madhvavijaya by Narayana Panditacharya – son of Trivikrama Pandita, who himself was a disciple of Madhva.

Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Madhvacharya.fact: The created universe is the dependent reality, consisting of Jīva (individual souls) and Jada (matter, material things).

Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Madhvacharya.fact: For liberation, mere intellectual conceptualization of Brahman as creator is not enough, the individual soul must feel attraction, love, attachment and devotional surrender to Him, and only His grace leads to redemption and liberation, according to Madhva. Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Madhvacharya.fact: He rejects monist theories believing that knowledge liberates, asserting instead that it is Divine grace through Bhakti that liberates.

Madhvacharya.fact: To Madhva, God obscures reality by creating Maya and Prakriti, which causes bondage and suffering; and only God can be the source of soul's release.

Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Madhvacharya.fact: Every Jiva (individual soul) is the agent of actions, not Jada (matter), and not Ishvara (God).

Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Madhvacharya.fact: Advaita's nondualism asserts that Atman (soul) and Brahman are blissful and identical, unchanging transcendent Reality, there is interconnected oneness of all souls and Brahman, with no pluralities. Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Madhvacharya.question: Of all schools, _____ directed his critique at Advaita most, penning four major texts, including Upadhikhandana and Tattvadyota, primarily dedicated to scrutinizing Advaita
Madhvacharya.fact: Madhvacharya was most ardent critic of Advaita Vedanta, accusing Shankara and the Advaitins of teaching Buddhism under the cover of Vedanta. Madhva, in contrast asserts that Atman (soul) and Brahman are different, only Vishnu is the Lord (Brahman), individual souls are also distinct and depend on Vishnu, and there are pluralities.

Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Madhvacharya.question: The Madhva Sampradaya fostered Bhakti and search of _____
Madhvacharya.fact: The Madhva Sampradaya fostered Bhakti and search of Knowledge.

Madhvacharya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Madhvacharya.fact: Such literature and works for critical thinking were written majorly in Sanskrit and not readily accessible to common people.

Mahabharata.question: In the _____ world, a well-known presentation of the epic is Peter Brook's nine-hour play, which premiered in Avignon in 1985, and its five-hour movie version The Mahābhārata
Mahabharata.fact: In the Western world, a well-known presentation of the epic is Peter Brook's nine-hour play, which premiered in Avignon in 1985, and its five-hour movie version The Mahābhārata.

Bhagavad Gita.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Bhagavad Gita.question: Swami Rambhadracharya released the first Braille version of the scripture, with the original Sanskrit text and a Hindi commentary, on _____ November 2007
Bhagavad Gita.fact: Swami Rambhadracharya released the first Braille version of the scripture, with the original Sanskrit text and a Hindi commentary, on 30 November 2007.
